newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania leu steady, unmoved by PM report.
newsitem.headline: Romania leu steady, unmoved by PM report.

text.p: Romania's leu currency closed flat on Friday at 5,950/980 to the dollar, unchanged from Thursday, and operators expect it to remain around this level over the next few days in a hard-currency-squeezed interbank market.
Traders said neither the market nor the leu had been moved by the grim report on the country's economy presented to reporters by Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea late on Thursday.
"The market is still digesting the news. However, it's hard to believe that the leu will slide to dramatic lows over the next few days," one said.

Ciorbea said Romania, which inherited a soaring inflation and a big budget deficit from the leftist government ousted in elections last November, was expected to have a negative economic growth this year.
It was Ciorbea's first assessment on the state of Romania's economy since the government started talks with international lenders, including the IMF, for fresh loans last week.
Operators said they expected the leu to hover around the present level "at least for two or three days."

Central bank governor Mugur Isarescu, who also attended Ciorbea's news conference, said the bank was preparing a package including steps to smooth out the interbank market, now plagued by chronic hard currency shortages.
Latest central bank data showed interbank trading since January 23 amounted to a daily average of $107,800, compared with an overall trading of $14.4 million on Thursday.

"The government has in some way to remove the rigidity of the foreign exchange market," said Mark Holdsworth, analyst with the London-based ING Barings bank, in reference to the the central bank's expected package.
On Friday, one-week funds were around 70 percent, slighlty higher than Thursday's level, operators said.
Leu-dollar retail rates stayed at about 6,000/200.
